issues.suggestion: Remove dangerouslySetInnerHTML and use a simple text node instead: {text}. If HTML rendering is required, use a sanitization library like DOMPurify:

codeQuality.summary: Critical XSS vulnerability from unsafe HTML rendering. This is a high-risk security issue that must be addressed immediately. Component also lacks performance optimizations and proper key props for list rendering.

issues.suggestion: Define a proper interface for Todo items: interface Todo { id: number; text: string; completed: boolean; } and use useState<Todo[]>([])

issues.description: Missing type annotation for 'id' parameter in deleteTodo function.

issues.description: Missing type annotation for 'id' parameter in toggleTodo function.

issues.description: getFilteredTodos function recalculates filtered todos on every render, even if filter hasn't changed. This causes unnecessary array iterations.
issues.suggestion: Memoize the filtered results using useMemo hook: const filteredTodos = useMemo(() => { ... }, [todos, filter])

Priority: (1) Add proper TypeScript types to eliminate 'any', (2) Memoize callbacks with useCallback and useMemo, (3) Extract filter predicates for testability, (4) Fix functional state updates, (5) Improve ID generation strategy.

recommendations.description: Fix XSS vulnerability in TodoItem.tsx by removing dangerouslySetInnerHTML and using plain text rendering instead. This is a severe security risk that allows script injection attacks.

Add comprehensive TypeScript type annotations throughout useTodos.ts. Replace 'any' types with proper interfaces for Todo items and function parameters. This will catch errors at compile time and improve maintainability.
Implement useCallback and useMemo optimizations in both files. Memoize callbacks in TodoItem and filter calculations in useTodos to prevent unnecessary re-renders in large todo lists.
Add comprehensive test coverage for both TodoItem component and useTodos hook. Start with critical path testing: component rendering, checkbox toggle, delete button, and core CRUD operations.
Extract reusable components and functions. Wrap TodoItem with React.memo, extract filter predicates to separate object, and use functional state updates to prevent stale closures.
Add input validation for edge cases. Implement max-length checks for todo text and use reliable ID generation (UUID or nanoid instead of Date.now()) to prevent collisions.
Ensure parent components pass key props to TodoItem when rendering in lists for proper React reconciliation. Add proper error handling and consider localStorage persistence layer.
